title: Ten commitments for a bold biotechnology industry - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Only the opening paragraph of this Comment is available in the captured text — the ten commitments promised by the title are behind the paywall, so the extractable signal is the framing, not the list. That framing: biotechnology is now a determinant of economic strength, national resilience and geopolitical influence, and the industry's binding constraint is eroding public trust and weakening scientific institutions. The piece is adapted from Ovid Therapeutics CEO Jeremy Levin's 2026 book 'Biotech in the Balance: Saving a Strategic Industry in an Age of Distrust'.

insights.claim: Biotechnology is framed as one of the defining technologies shaping economic strength, national resilience and geopolitical influence over the coming decades — placing it alongside semiconductors and AI in the strategic-industry category rather than treating it as a healthcare vertical.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Strategic-industry framing is the precursor to industrial policy: expect onshoring incentives, export controls and sovereign biomanufacturing funds to become live catalysts for the sector.
insights.quote: As biotechnology becomes one of the defining technologies that will shape economic strength, national resilience and geopolitical influence over the coming decades

insights.claim: The argument treats the industry as something that needs 'saving' as a strategic asset, per the source book's subtitle 'Saving a Strategic Industry in an Age of Distrust', implying the author sees current trajectory as decline rather than ascent.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A sitting biotech CEO publishing a rescue narrative rather than a growth narrative is a sentiment marker for how insiders read the sector's funding and policy environment in 2026.
insights.locator: Acknowledgements; References, Biotech in the Balance

insights.claim: The stated priority for the industry is rebuilding and preserving public trust, positioned as a prerequisite rather than a reputational nicety — trust, not capital or science, is presented as the scarce input.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If trust is the constraint, pricing behavior, transparency and vaccine-adjacent political risk become first-order valuation inputs for drug developers, not ESG footnotes.
insights.quote: the industry must commit to rebuilding and preserving public trust

insights.claim: The trust problem is attributed to growing pressures on the institutions that underpin scientific leadership, locating the risk in the research and regulatory apparatus rather than in individual companies' conduct.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Institutional degradation — funding cuts, regulatory capacity, agency credibility — becomes a sector-wide risk factor that no single company can hedge, arguing for policy-tracking as part of biotech underwriting.
insights.quote: in the face of growing pressures on the institutions that underpin scientific leadership

insights.claim: The captured article text contains only the abstract-length framing plus front matter; the ten commitments named in the title never appear, so any downstream use of this record should not assume the prescriptive content was analyzed.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Flags this card as low-content: the actionable list is behind a subscription and would need the book or the full Comment to evaluate.
insights.quote: This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution

insights.claim: The Comment is an excerpt adapted from a commercially published book by the same author, meaning the piece functions partly as promotion for Rodin Books' 2026 release rather than as standalone primary analysis.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Discount the piece's novelty accordingly; the substantive argument lives in the book, and the author declares no competing interests despite the promotional overlap.
insights.quote: This Comment is excerpted and adapted from Biotech in the Balance: Saving a Strategic Industry in an Age of Distrust by J.M.L.
